headline: Wilderness Permit and Campground Availability Check
reservation: Most trails and sites do not require day-use permits, but Northwest Forest Passes are required at designated trailheads. Reservations for popular campgrounds like Diamond Lake or North Umpqua should be made via Recreation.gov well in advance; verify current fire restrictions and road closures with the Forest Service.

days.title: The Highway of Waterfalls

stops.name: Toketee Falls
stops.detail: View the two-tiered fall pouring through a natural basalt column doorway via a short forest trail.

stops.name: Watson Falls
stops.detail: Hike to the base of one of Oregon's highest plunges, standing at 272 feet amidst a misty canyon.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes for travel along OR-138; mountain roads can be narrow.
days.note: Expect wet and slippery boardwalks near waterfall viewpoints; sturdy footwear is recommended.

days.title: High Cascade Peaks

stops.name: Diamond Lake
stops.detail: Engage in water activities or cycle the 11-mile paved loop with views of Mt. Bailey and Mt. Thielsen.

stops.name: Clearwater Falls
stops.detail: Observe the unique spring-fed falls that emerge directly from mossy rocks rather than a traditional stream.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; check for seasonal snow closures on higher elevation spurs.
days.note: Mosquito activity is significant near the lake from June through early August.

days.title: Old Growth and River Confluences

stops.name: Colliding Rivers
stops.detail: Witness the rare geological phenomenon where the North Umpqua and Little Rivers meet head-on.

stops.name: Susan Creek Falls
stops.detail: Walk the accessible 1.5-mile trail through old-growth Douglas fir to a 50-foot moss-lined cascade.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; transit between lower forest sites is generally straightforward.
days.note: Check the Forest Service website for local alerts regarding the North Umpqua Trail segments.

intel.title: Trailhead Pass Requirements
intel.text: Many waterfall trailheads require a Northwest Forest Pass or daily fee. Parking lots at Toketee and Watson Falls can fill by midday during summer weekends.

intel.title: Corridor Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is nonexistent for most of OR-138 between Glide and Diamond Lake. Download offline maps and emergency contact info before leaving Roseburg.

intel.title: Glide to Diamond Lake Gap
intel.text: Fuel is available in Glide and at the Diamond Lake Resort, but there are no stations in the 60-mile stretch between them. Always start the day with a full tank.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Access
intel.text: Higher elevation roads near Mt. Thielsen may remain snow-covered until late June. Check the ODOT TripCheck service for real-time mountain pass conditions.

intel.title: Fire and Trail Closures
intel.text: Wildfire activity can lead to sudden forest closures in late summer. Verify air quality and trail status on the official Umpqua National Forest alerts page.

plan.arrival: Fly into MFR and drive two hours north to Roseburg for supplies. Proceed east to Glide for park check-in or campsite setup.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for forest service roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Watch the sunset over Diamond Lake to see the reflection of Mt. Thielsen, depending on cloud cover and season.
